FOREWORD

Standard ( Part I ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 23 June lC82, after the draft finalized by the Electromechanical Components for Electronic Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard ( Part I ) was originally revision has been brought out to take account developments and experience gained through standard since its first publication. published in 1967. This of the latest technology the implementation of the

0.3 This standard ( Part I ) covers general requirements and tests The specific requirements appliccommon to various types of terminals. able to particular types of terminals are specified in the relevant specifications forming subsequent parts of this standard. 0.4 While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from JSS 52710-1974 `Specification for terminals, captive screw cap and captive spring loaded' issued by the Directorate of Standardization, Ministry of Defence, India. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this or calculated, standard is complied with, the final value, observed expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in actordThe number of significant plates retained in ante with IS : 2-1960*. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part I ) covers general requirements and tests for terminals ( sealed and non-sealed ) for use in electronics and telecommunication equipment. . 1.2 This standard does not apply to system terminals, such as, transmitter terminals and receiver terminals. 2. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-df fined system of inspection, testing and quality IS1 control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safcyguard. 8.6 Voltage Proof ( for Insulated Terminals Only ) - The specimen shall be moun:ed on a suitable metal plate in the normal manner. An ac test voltage of a frequency 50 Hz Thall be applied between the terminal and mounting plate for 1 min for typi: approval test and for 5 s for acceptance test. The relationship between the rated valtage, UR ( rms ) and the test voltage, E ( rms ) is given below: For terminals E = 2 lJR f For terminals E =- 500 V The voltage shall be steadily increased from zero to the proof value at a rate of approximately 500 V per second. Upon completion of the test, the proof voltage shall be gradually reduced to avoid voltage surges. There

8.7 Insulation Resistance ( for Insulated Terminals Only ) The specimen shall be mounted on a suitable metal plate in the normal manner. The insulation resistance shall he rneasured at 100 & 15 V or 500 h 50 V as specified in the relevant specification. The voltage shall be applied for 1 minute f 5 seconds ( or less if a stable reading has been obtained ) between the terminal and the mounting piate. The insulation resistance shall be read at the end of that period.

The contact resistance shall then be measured between the terminal and the closest exposed portion of the conductor with a dc voltage source, the open A circuit voltage of which does not exceed 2.5 V and a current of 1 A. 40/O-2 mm conc'uctor insulated with PVC 0.6 mm thick shall be used for spike type of terminal. The contact resistance value shall not exceed 5 milliohms.

8.18 Cap Spring Pressure ( for Spring Loaded Terminals Only ) - The specimen shall be mounted on a suitable metal plate in tht normal manner. The cap shall be depressed to its maximum position by applying an axial compressive force in the centre of the cap top. The pressure shall then be gradually released at the rate of 18 N per minute. When the tap has returned approximately 0.4 mm from its fully depressed concition, the remaining spring pressure shall be recorded. The cap spring pressure shall be not more than 22 N and not less than 14 N. 8.19 Cap Retention ( for Spring Loaded Terminals Only ) - The specimen shall be held in a fixed Fosition by gripping the upper half of the cap. A suitable gripping device shall be used.
